judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: Teaser photo in the NEWS section, alt = the headline "Fight on to save busy Wetherspoons in the North East as pub's future in doubt". The crop shows an empty pub interior (bar, chequered floor, chairs): the alt names the subject shown (a Wetherspoons pub) but the campaign, the doubt and 'busy' are not in the picture, so the claim holds as worded. The snapshot gave the image a height of 0 (lazy load at capture time), but the crop shows the real image, so the model judged the right picture. The image is not inside a link: the teaser's headline is a separate link (with an aria-label equal to the headline) right below it, so R2 does not apply. Whether a headline used as the alt of an illustrative teaser photo fails 1.1.1 is disputed among competent auditors: one reading treats the photo as informative and requires the alt to convey what it shows; another treats it as illustrating the adjacent headline, where the headline-as-alt is redundant (axe ranks redundant alt text as best practice, not a WCAG failure) and the alt still names the story the photo stands for; a third calls the photo decorative and would want alt="" (F38). The evidence cannot settle which purpose the photo serves, so elementFails is cannot_tell and the label is uncertain. The live server HTML has the same img, alt and src, so the capture matches.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: h3 inside the headline link of an affiliate 'shopwindow' teaser (mirror.co.uk) placed in the NUFC section. The content under the heading, before the next heading (h2 UNMISSABLE), is only the teaser's source label 'mirror.co.uk'; the heading names the very article its own teaser links to (a mirror.co.uk shopping-deals story about the shampoo). Nothing under it is about a different topic, so the claim is false; that the teaser is off-topic for the NUFC section is a placement choice, not a 2.4.6 failure, since the h3 describes its own content. The affiliate widget is injected client-side and is absent from the live server HTML, so I could not compare it live; nothing suggests the capture differed from what users got at capture time.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: SVG image 'C SUBSCRIBE' with alt="nechronicle" (the site's internal code name), the only content of the header link to /subscribe. The claim is true of the capture: the alt names a label and omits the word SUBSCRIBE shown in the image. But the link carries aria-label="Subscribe to premium membership", which is the control's accessible name (ARIA8/ARIA6) and overrides the image's alt, so assistive technology announces the link's purpose, not 'nechronicle'. For non-text content that is a control, 1.1.1 asks that it have a name that describes its purpose, and the link does; unlike a title (R2), aria-label is the name itself. The packet gave the link's name, so the model had the context. The button is rendered by script and is not in the live server HTML, so I could not compare it live; the screenshot matches the snapshot.
